utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning to you all. Would you please convey to Ms. Somers the condolences of the Chamber on the death of her father.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I most certainly well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you ready to call the --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Before I start, I inform the Trial Chamber that at some point today, the three psychiatrists engaged by the Prosecution to examine the accused, Mr. Strugar, may be present in the public gallery at some point. I don't know when. The next Prosecution witness is Ms. Zineta Ogresta. I call her.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning, to you. If you would be kind enough to take the affirmation from the card there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you like to sit down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Good morning, Ms. Ogresta. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber your full name.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: My name is Zineta Ogresta. My maiden name is Dilberovic. I was born on the 30th of December in 1950 in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And do you still live in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, unfortunately I do. In the hotel. I still have not returned to my own home.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what is your occupation?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I am now pensioned. I have invalidity, disability pension because I suffered from cancer of the breast. Otherwise, I was an administrator in the health service.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you living in Dubrovnik in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, since I was born.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you living in October, November, and up until the 6th of December, 1991? Just the address, please.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Od Sigurate number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And where is that in relation to the Festival Palace?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It's opposite the Festival Palace. The Festival Palace is number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's in the Old Town, of course?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was your occupation in October, November, December 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: My occupation was in the microbiological laboratory of the Dubrovnik health service, and in October when that unfortunate terrible war began who nobody liked, who brought us much suffering, terrible, I worked in the laboratory then. However, straight after the beginning of the war, we moved the old hospital to Medarevo when the first sirens sounded, and then we went to Medarevo to work there in the new hospital. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were both those health facilities outside the Old Town located in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, outside the Old Town but in Dubrovnik proper.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I will be showing you some photographs a little bit later of your house, but I want you to tell the Trial Chamber at the moment how many levels did the house in which you were living have?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Two floors, the ground floor and the attic. So four levels in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's three floors and an attic?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. Starting at the bottom, what was on the ground floor?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: On the ground floor there was a warehouse belonging to a shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What sort of shop?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It sold footwear. I think it was the Obuca Beograd company and later on the Alpina company, but they tended to change rather fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your house was located on the corner of Od Sigurate and Stradun; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes. To the north-western part, the north-western section looking at it from the Stradun, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the shop or the warehouse on the ground floor, did it have an entrance onto Stradun, a commercial entrance onto Stradun?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it did, on the southern front. That's where the entrance to the shop was, and the storage space was on the ground floor in our house as soon as you entered that building to the left.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In which street, Od Sigurate or Stradun?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, Stradun. That's where the entrance to the shop was, and my entrance was in the street, Od Sigurate number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll take you to the first floor. That's the second level of the house. What was on the first level -- sorry, the first floor, the second level?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: On the first floor was a wonderful stone - how shall I put this? - stone shelves, because it was a house belonging to the nobility before. So this was a wonderful stone wall which should have been protected like the whole of Dubrovnik under UNESCO protection, because I thought -- I think that it was highly valuable culturally speaking, this stone edifice.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On the first floor was a shop or commercial space. On the next two levels up, was that residential?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, it was residential. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did anyone live on the first floor?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: There was a lady. Her name was Matic, and she lived there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Matic. What was her first name?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Mrs. Marija Matic, Mrs. Marija Matic.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many rooms were on the first floor?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I'm not quite sure. Perhaps four. Perhaps four plus the bathroom and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When was Ms. Matic born?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Mrs. Matic, Mrs. Marija Matic, was born in 1900 -- 1910, actually, so she was 81 at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who lived on the second floor?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I did with my mother -- with my sister. I'm sorry. With my nephew, his wife, and just one more child.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you were born in 1950. Were you 40 as of the 6th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, 40. Well, actually my birthday was on the 30th of December, so just a few days short of 40.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think you mean 41. You said that you were a -- you worked in a hospital and the health clinic -- and a health clinic in 1991. Were you in the military in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, no. I was exclusively a civilian.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've just mentioned your sister. How old was your sister in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was her occupation in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: She wasn't working at the time. Otherwise, she had a boutique at Babin Kuk, and she ran the boutique with a colleague, another lady. She did sewing, designed clothes, that kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was she in the military in 19 -- December 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, never. She doesn't know what the military is at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your nephew was also living with you. How old was your nephew?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. He was 33 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was his occupation in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: He worked at a printing press not far from Dubrovnik, in Zupa, but that printing house -- actually, the first shelling began outside Dubrovnik, and it was razed to the ground, destroyed completely, and he was left without a job.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was he in the military in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, not at all. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about your nephew's wife? How old was she, and what was her occupation in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: 30, I think. Yes, about 30, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what did she do?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: She worked in bookkeeping in the centre for social welfare.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was she in the military?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You also had a child living with you. Who was the child?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. The child's name was Deni, Deni Dilberovic, and he was four when the war began.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is he your great nephew, that is, the child of your nephew and his wife.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why was your nephew and your -- and his wife and their son living with you in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: They lived there all the time because my father had the right of tenant in the apartment, so in that system that was the socialist system, you would inherit this -- these tenant's rights. So after my father it went to my mother. After her death it went to my sister, and we all lived together because it was a big apartment, about 250 square metres with the attic space. We all lived together and then they remained living there, stayed on. They lived there since birth like us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Who actually owned the building or owns the building?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, this is how it was: The building had several owners. One of the main proprietors, and I assume the proprietor of our actual apartment was Mrs. Ljiljana Bulic, and she lived in Split, and she inherited the house, and a part of it belonged to the Murati family, and there are many family members there but they have a very small section, perhaps 1/16th of the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And did your family occupy the second floor, that's the third level of this building, and the loft?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which side of the building was the loft, the Stradun side or the Od Sigurate side?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Both facing Stradun and the Od Sigurate side.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What could you see if you looked out the window from the loft on the Stradun side? What was your view of?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I always looked at Srdj, Mount Srdj, because that's where most of the shelling took place. Somebody would shoot a shell. There would be smoke. It was terrible. I don't know who.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you looked out the window of the loft on the Od Sigurate side, what were you looking at or what could you see?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I could see the Hotel Imperijal.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to describe for the Trial Chamber the interior of the building, the staircases and the rooms. Firstly starting with the staircases. Can you describe what they looked like in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I would go in through the main hallway, and on the left-hand side straight ahead was the side entrance to the boutique. To the left was the door to the warehouse or the storage space, and also to the left when you go on there were four steps. We call them skalini, and there would be a narrow space there, I don't know how many square metres, not more than three square metres, maybe even smaller, and then you would have one staircase, a wooden staircase, up to the first floor or, rather, the second landing, and then there were wooden stairs. I've almost forgotten. You know, it's been 13 years and I don't wish to remember it either. But, yes, there was a wooden staircase leading up to my own floor, and on that upper storey, I can't describe the first floor very well because I never went to Mrs. Marija's apartment, but my own apartment had eight rooms. We had a large hall, high ceilings, and it was all built in the old way, the way of -- the buildings were built in Dubrovnik. And on my level there was a credenzija [phoen]. We had a veranda. It was a very artistically built interior and building. It was a wonderful building, a real palace.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber has heard of a number of buildings in Dubrovnik described as palaces which were in fact houses. Was your house one of those buildings?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, that's absolutely correct. And there were two coats of arms. One of them was slightly damaged but not much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You mentioned high ceilings. Did the rooms had beams?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. There were beams. Perhaps it would have been different had it been a stone solid -- more solid surface.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On the veranda, did the veranda have a balustrade?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes. It was very ornamental, the balustrade with pillars in the baroque style.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How would you describe the quality of the interior of your house or palace in comparison to other buildings in Dubrovnik in the Old Town that you've been in?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't want to be immodest, if I say that it was one of the most beautiful apartments, the one that my father received, but through many years of work, we made it even more beautiful. We made a large loft with a chimney piece, a mantle piece, and it was very beautiful, and we would rent out to foreigners, and they were always surprised to see how beautiful it was. It was very imposing. For example, the sitting room, the salon, was 30 square metres, and the other rooms did too. They had a soul, if I can put it that way, but perhaps I just felt that, but that's what I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And were there any small decorative touches to the finishes, cabinets or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. I've already said that there was a wall, decorative wooden sculptured set of shelves.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that built into the wall as part of the building?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes, it was like a built-in cupboard.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In December 1991, approximately how many people were living in Od Sigurate? That's the street.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: 17, 20 people perhaps. But otherwise, the street is empty now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were these people military, civilians?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Civilians, exclusively civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the age of the people, the age mixture of the people living in the street then?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Ranging from 50 to 70. Mrs. Marija, of course, was 81.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were there any other children in the street apart from your nephew Deni?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, there were other children. Two, four, six -- six children. There were some who came from elsewhere, because first the shelling started out of town. There were detonations there, and then people came to Dubrovnik to stay with their families there. Many of them thought, and we thought, too, that that was the safest place to be, that Dubrovnik was an old city, well-protected, and safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the ages of these six children?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: My nephew's son was four, and these other children, well, there were two who were about three or four as well, and two were teenagers, 13 or 12, something like that, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just to clarify your previous answer, you said there were some who came from elsewhere. Are you saying -- I'm sorry. I withdraw that. How many of those children had come in to stay with relatives and how many lived permanently in the street before the shelling started?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Five children lived there continuously, whereas those who came during the war, well, there were about two of them, I think, but then I'm not too sure because we don't have such close ties, I mean the upper and the lower parts of the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've told the Trial Chamber about shelling. When did the shelling start?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: The 1st of October, 1991. Again I got up in the morning. A friend of mine came to spend the night with me, and we were getting ready to go to work, and my sister was too, and we heard some detonations. And it wasn't too far away and then it was getting closer and closer. I was so surprised. And then I wondered what was going on. I thought it was the garbage trucks, and I wondered how come they were so loud that morning. But no. Then I looked out through the window and I saw there was no one was there, and I said, "My God, the war has started." And then I got ready to go to work, and then I heard the siren. However, I went because it was my duty to help people, although I worked in the administration. But I did go to work. When I got to work, the shelling started. This aircraft flying so low, and Srdj was targeted with a cluster bomb. My goodness. I thought this was a movie, as if it weren't true. It was as if this was a movie, this horror movie right in front of my own eyes, a -- and I never even liked such movies. It was terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you identify the aircraft that was targeting Srdj? Which side did it belong to?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: The Yugoslav People's Army, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember any damage to the Old Town as a result of shelling on the 1st of October?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think Sponza was targeted too, and then St. Blaise church was hit. It underwent reconstruction then. Then the Franciscan cloister was targeted then too, I think, and then afterwards on the 6th of December, 1991, and that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I'm only asking you about the 1st of October at the moment. Now, there was shelling on the 1st of October. Was there any other shelling that you remember in October?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: There were many. Then the Rupe museum was hit too. I remember that, but the date, I mean I have really forgotten the date. I didn't write down the dates. My husband did. He wrote down all the dates, but I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about November? Do you remember any occasions of shelling in the Old Town in November? If you don't, please feel free to say you don't remember.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I will tell you that there was shelling in October and in November. I can't remember the exact dates, but there was shelling certainly. We did not go into the shelter because we had this terrible aversion towards it. It was awful. Then we sought shelter at the neighbours across the street, because his door was firmer and there was an agency there. So that's where we tried to hide. I don't know. But we went there all the time instead of to the shelter, the regular shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'd ask you to pause there. You've mentioned shelters. Where was the nearest shelter to your house on corner of Stradun and Od Sigurate?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Minceta, Fort Minceta, which is again rock solid. I was an optimist all my life, but that didn't come to much, did it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you spend the night of the 5th of December, 1991, in your house on Od Sigurate too?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. But every evening there was a bit of gunfire. They were really taking it out on us. They wanted to frighten us. They were shooting all the time. For a while I couldn't even sleep because of these detonations. My window would get all lit up. I mean, I'm not really very knowledgeable about these military things, but these bullets, the ones that would light up everything, they would wake me up. What was that, sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just interrupting you, asking you to pause. I'm going to take you through what happened on the 6th of December, but I just want you to listen to the question and follow -- and follow it in a sequence.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You just told the Trial Chamber you spent the night of the 5th of December at your home. I want to move to what happened the next morning. What time did you wake up?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Very early. Detonations woke me up. I was getting ready, in spite of everything, to go to work. At that time I worked in Medarevo. However, the detonations were stronger and stronger. And then I changed my clothes. I put on my house clothes and my clogs, but everything started very early. First I looked through the window and --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just go back. The question was, what time did you wake up?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, around 5.30 approximately. Early. Early. Before 6.00. It must have been before 6.00. I can't remember exactly now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could you describe the volume of the detonations that you heard when you woke up.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Oh, very strong, very strong at first. Very strong.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were they coming from? Could you say from which direction they were coming from?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It seemed to me that they were coming from all sides. I really can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you looked at the window. Which window did you go to?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: The window of Sigurate number 2. So that's the western side. I looked through the window, and I saw that Srdj was being shelled, and there were very strong detonations. But house is close to this hill, Srdj.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was it light or dark when you woke up?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, it was sort of half dark. It was already dawning or, rather, it had already dawned but not completely. So you couldn't see much. Well, we couldn't see much because we had no electricity or water, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was it that led you to conclude that Srdj was being shelled? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, it was targeted, it was hit, and all of a sudden I saw this fire, this explosion, this terrible explosion. I don't know how to describe this, this terrible noise. And then dust went up as if something had been blown up sort of.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go from your window?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. My sister insisted that we go downstairs, that it was safer at the first level of this house of ours, but I didn't want to go. As a matter of fact, I took a book to read because I said, "No, no." And then she said, "Let's take some photographs. Let's do something about this, perhaps even the worst can happen to us." And I said, "No, no," but then we did go downstairs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did you remain downstairs?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, you see, it seems to me that it was 45 years. Perhaps it was 45 minutes or something like that. Anyway, we went down there around 6.00 o'clock, and we were there for about 45 minutes in this small space.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the explosions? Were they continuing?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Continuing, yes, yes, and getting stronger and stronger.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where was your nephew that day?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: My nephew, with his wife and his young son, had left ten days before that. They went to Boninovo. That is to say, Branka Dilberovic went to stay with her mother Veronika Vera. This is near the Boninovo cemetery.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were your sister and -- sorry. Was your nephew and his wife there that day?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Fortunately not. Otherwise, they all would have gotten killed, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do as the explosions became stronger and stronger?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: We went downstairs. I just took my jacket. Because it was so noisy that, first of all, I thought I'd go deaf. I thought that if I lived through that, I could never hear again. Shells were falling incessantly above our heads, and there is this small window within this space, and it is a barred window.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I need you to describe for the Trial Chamber exactly where you went to. You said you went downstairs. Where did you -- where is downstairs, on which level of the four levels of your house?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: The ground floor. The ground floor where the shop is and where the warehouse is, where the very entrance into the house is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On Od Sigurate or Stradun?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Od Sigurate number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You have a doorway onto the street?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And do the stairs lead from the street to the first and second floors?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, not from the street. When you enter that house, there are stairs that take you upstairs. So the stairs are further up. And we enter on the right-hand side, and then we have some stairs within the house itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The space where you were with your sister, is that just behind the door as you come in before the stairs?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: After four stairs comes the narrow space near this small window, the one with bars on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How big is that space approximately?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't think that there is more than two square metres, perhaps even less than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, you said you went there with your sister. Now what about Mrs. Matic? Where was she?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: As for Mrs. Marija Matic, we first visited her at her apartment. We brought her to the place where we were hiding too. The lady was quite elderly. Had we left her there on her own, she certainly could not have survived.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How mobile was she at the age of 81 in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I'll tell you, she was quite mobile. Perhaps she may even be alive today. She was still around a year ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: There were three of you in this space several steps up from the street level. What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: What did we do? We were standing there. We couldn't even move our hands left or right, and we were praying to God for all of this to pass, and we wondered why, why all of this was happening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the shelling that you described earlier as continuing and getting stronger? What was happening with the shelling when you were standing there with Mrs. Matic and your sister?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Above our heads. So that's the western side of our house above our heads nonstop from all directions. From the sea, I think, and I don't know, from the land, from everywhere, within split seconds. It was awful. It was truly awful.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What could you hear?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I heard this noise, and I even saw this - what do you call it? - shrapnel, yes, shrapnel. If I had moved my hand or my arm, I would have been hit for sure. It was like a torrent.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How loud was the sound of the exploding of the shells from where you were standing?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Terrible. I don't know how many decibels, really, but it was unbearable, it defied description. I put my jacket on my ears, and I was trembling in this small space there. There was no future for us. If we stayed there, we'd got killed. If we went out, we'd got killed. So there was nothing for us to do. We were in the hand of God.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said there was shrapnel. What did you see or hear?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I saw and heard shrapnel. I heard them and saw them falling like a torrent, like rain. This is the ground floor, and then there is this small window with bars, and shells were falling and shrapnel was all around, and it was by sheer chance that not a single piece of shrapnel hit us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you see of this shrapnel when you looked out the window?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I saw shrapnel made of lead flying at this terrible speed coming from all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How long did you stay in that space with your sister and Mrs. Matic?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think I've already said this. About 45 minutes approximately. I don't know exactly. That is just an approximation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was your building hit?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, from all sides. It was these guided missiles. Not once. It seems to me that all of those that fell in town fell on our home.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How do you know your -- I'm sorry. Was your building hit when you were in the space with Mrs. Matic and your sister?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you hear? What did you -- what did you feel? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: We heard noise. I've already said this. Terrible noise, these detonations as if they were hammering into our heads. We felt like we were having a heatstroke. We thought that we were finished. I already said that if I moved my hand or arm, if I moved in that small space I would have been hit by this because we saw this torrent of shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you were downstairs, what was happening upstairs in your building?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: At one moment there was destruction. The walls were probably caving in. The plaster started falling, and there was this terrible smoke. We thought that we would die the most terrible of deaths, that we would be killed within this very own house of ours that we took such good care of. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you hear happening upstairs?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Upstairs there was this terrible destruction. I don't know. I heard that things were breaking. It's as if it were an earthquake. Perhaps I can put it that way. And I cannot tell you exactly how strong. So everything was caving in and we were in this tiny space.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What happened to the stairs?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Part of the staircase was totally destroyed. So later on when my sister wanted to go upstairs, she couldn't go upstairs because half of the staircase was destroyed. So she simply couldn't get there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said things were breaking upstairs and it felt like an earthquake and you were standing near the stairs. Did anything come down the stairs towards you?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Yes. Yes, plaster. Plaster, stone. There was so much dust. It was impossible. You could hardly see a thing downstairs. You could hardly breathe. We needed gas masks in order not to suffocate. As a matter of fact, we had even reconciled ourselves to the fact that we would die.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you felt like we were having a heatstroke. What do you mean by that? Describe what you felt.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It was so hot. I'm not really knowledgeable about these things, but we felt so hot in the face that it was impossible. We felt that way. It felt like a heatstroke. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How did you get out of there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: This is the way it was: I was praying to God. I was listening to all of this, and all of a sudden I heard a voice. I still hear this voice until the present day every now and then. "Zineta, Zineta." It was a neighbour, and we had become friends only shortly before that. This was the husband of a neighbour and friend, Mr. Vladimir Srhoj. They got married just before that, and I heard him calling out to me, "Zineta." And I said, "Yes." And he got out of his apartment, and we opened the door. There was still shooting going on all the time. The house had not been set on fire yet. So we went out of the house with Mrs. Marija, and it was Mr. Vladimir who helped us. We went out on the street. It was terrible out there on the street. We were walking on shards of glass and stone and rocks, all sorts of construction material debris. We were so worried what would happen to us then. We got to an apartment. I already said that it was a rather firmly built apartment. So that was our salvation. However, when we came there hoping that we would be rescued in that way, again a shell fell. Unfortunately, it did not go down all the way. It made a hole in the roof. We hid in the downstairs toilet, and again we felt this heatstroke, this redness. It threw us. It was quite unbelievable. And then -- well, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that Mr. Vladimir Srhoj's apartment that you went to?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the ground floor. Not the actual apartment where he lived but the ground floor of that house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What number is it in the street?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think it is Od Sigurate number 4, not 5, because the festival building is 1, we are 2, then -- now, let me think. 4 or 5. 4 or 5, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You mentioned before that your building was not on fire when you went to Mr. Srhoj's place. What happened to your building?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: After that, these guided missiles came right through the window from the western side and the southern side. This is an inflammatory missile, I think. So the house was hit, and it started burning. It was first the curtains that started burning. There were beautiful curtains from Venice. I wish I still had photographs of that house. I wish I had taken that out. But within a few seconds, everything burnt down. Our entire lives. I felt as if I had lost my identity. My family, people who lived with me, all my memories, all of our memories. Terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where were you when your house was hit by the shell that caused it to burn down?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: In front. We were in front of that house, the house belonging to my neighbour Mr. Vladimir Srhoj. We stood there and watched what was happening, and there was shooting all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you -- I just want you to tell the Trial Chamber what you saw in terms of a missile or a shell going through the window? Which window was it?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: From the western side on the second floor, rather, the third level. It was a direct hit, and I assume that it was an incendiary shell because it set fire to it. Now, the house had been practically destroyed and now this finished it off, by setting fire to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the Festival Palace? Was it on fire at that point?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Not at that point, no, but sometime later it was set fire to as well. It was aflame. And one of our neighbours had a well, and we tried to use the water because there wasn't otherwise any water, but we tried to do what we could with these cans of water. We tried to save our own house. That was impossible. And our neighbour's house, but we did manage to save one house which follows on from our neighbour's house, because the fire didn't spread after that. From the Od Sigurate and the Kantun street by the festival house, we were able to control the fire from spreading. And we were all involved, men and women, and it was very difficult because there was shooting and shelling on all sides. Our hair was on fire, but we were in a state of shock. I really don't know. I can't say. We did what we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: About what time did your house catch fire?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think it was about 10.00 o'clock. Around 10.00. But of course we lost all track of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did fire-fighters come when your house --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. They came urgently, it was an emergency. But unfortunately we weren't able to save anything. We were left completely naked. I was wearing my slippers or clogs, and it was a very cold day, and we felt the cold even more in our hearts.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In case it wasn't clear before, you said a -- just to clarify something, you said a shell hit your neighbour's roof. That's Mr. Srhoj's roof. Can you describe the damage to his house by that shell?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It didn't cause great damage, but it made a roof -- a hole in the roof. So it was minor damage, and he was able to deal with it himself and repair it.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And in case I missed something before, were you inside the ground floor of his building when it hit or were you outside?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Inside. Inside at that time. Inside in the ground floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you do after your house burnt down?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Nothing. We -- well, we tried to put the fire out. We didn't succeed, and then went back to our neighbour's ground floor and waited there helpless. We stayed until the evening. We lost all track of time. As I said, we didn't know when it was day, night. We lost our orientation in space, in time. And then Mrs. Branka Dilberovic's brother came to fetch us, Mladen was his name, and took us off to his house at Boninovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When did you return to the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: On the 7th, in the morning. We were in shock.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where did you go?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: We went back to the place that we had experienced those terrible moments. Stradun looked terrible. The street looked terrible. Every house looked dreadful. And everything was damaged to one house, destroyed. Just four walls remained standing.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You went back to your street where you lived for years. Was the street damaged? I'm sorry, were buildings in the street damaged apart from your own?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think they were, but I looked at mine mostly. The Od Puca Street was badly damaged, and the Mala Braca church. That was hit too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was there damage to the walls of the houses in Od Puca?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What did you see? Describe the damage.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: You mean on my own house or the houses in the Od Puca Street?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In Od Puca Street.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, the same thing. Everything was burnt. The window frames were black. The glass shattered. The frames broken, just like on our own house. It had burnt down completely. Several of them, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that in Od Puca Street or in your street that several houses had burnt down?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Od Puca Street was also -- there were also several houses there which had burnt down like our house. However, on the Stradun there were only two houses like that, the Festival Palace building and our own house. They were in that state, a sorry state.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Going back to your own street and the damage to houses in Od Puca -- in Od Sigurate Street. Can you describe generally the damage to buildings, windows, doors in that street? Leaving your own house out for the moment.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: My neighbour's roof. And then in my street the monastery. There was major damage there, but that was up above. It's the same street, but you go up some stairs, and it's the second half of the street on the left opposite me. This was the highest point. And the monastery was damaged there, and it suffered heavy damage during the war. As far as I remember, there wasn't any other damage in our street.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You described earlier hearing or seeing shrapnel in the street when you were in the space near the stairs. Did you see anything to indicate that shrapnel had fallen in the street?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, it was a torrent of shrapnel, and if that was the case, it fell on the street, where else?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see any damage to any buildings as a result of that -- from that shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: You mean mine or other buildings, other houses?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm only talking about the street at the moment.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Oh, I see, the street. No, I didn't notice that or as much.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to describe the state of your own house when you came back on the 7th of December. What did you see?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, it was like this: You could see the sky up above, so all that remained standing were the four walls. The windows were all black or, rather, the window frames were all black. They were split quite a bit on the second and first floor, from the west and on the southern side as well. And on the south, the door frames had burnt down completely as well as part of the stone. It was all black. As you know -- I don't know how stone burns, but anyway, it was all black. I don't know if it was burnt. And then from the south side, there was a vertical crack, a very large vertical crack from the windows of the first floor to the roof. And as far as I remember now, whether that is correct or not, but this is how I remember it, from -- on the western side there was large vertical crack, once again, on the walls. And inside everything had burnt down to the ground. So the house was completely burnt down on the inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And just so we're clear, the Od Sigurate Street is the western side and Stradun is the southern side; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the Festival Palace? Describe the damage you saw to the Festival Palace.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, it was in the same state, like our house mostly. As for the details, I really can't remember. I was more interested in my own house. I saw that it had been burnt, but I can't tell you about the details. I didn't remember any.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you two clips from a video which is in evidence, that is P78, which was tendered during Mr. Jusic's evidence. And for the record, I'm showing the witness a clip starting at time at 23:40 seconds.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the festival building. That's the Manon [phoen] cafe. That's my house with the coat of arms, that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's at 24:13.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes. That's the house. You -- this is what Dubrovnik looked like on the 7th of December. Here you have it. See for yourselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We move now to the second clip. The time at 25:13.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Again, is that a view of your house and the Festival Palace?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. That's the festival building.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: 25:39. Can you indicate what street that is at 25:56 or 57?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think that was my street. Od Sigurate I think that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: They're very short clips. I'll just play the two through again starting with clip one, and I want you to tell the Trial Chamber the different -- if you can see the different floors.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the festival building. Uh-huh, uh-huh, uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just for the record, we're going back to the first clip.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Uh-huh. That's the boutique. That's the ground floor of the festival building. Uh-huh. This is my building, was my building.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Stop there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We just stopped at 24:10. Is that the --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Ten, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that the first floor of the building where Mrs. Matic lived?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, the first floor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You can --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Except -- I apologise. The windows faced west. So on the first floor, Dr. Pjerotic had his surgery, and there was another family, one of the proprietors, actually, the Murati family, so that was part of their section, but they lived there for a short time and left. Of course Mrs. Matic lived in Od Sigurate, too, facing the street, facing number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just looking at what we can see on the screen, is the top two floors and the loft or the attic part.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Two windows at the top, and this is at time 24:19. The top two floors, the top two windows, was that where you lived?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the loft we can see above the third window to the right. Was that your loft?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. That was our neighbour's, belonged to one of our neighbours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is your loft no longer there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And the view we're looking at is looking from Stradun onto your building; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You described a shell going through a window. Was it one of the windows we can see in this particular still?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Which one do you think it was?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think it was the first one, the left one.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's so black.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've just stopped it at 24:28. There's a man standing in front of two windows on the ground floor. Is that the commercial premises, the warehouse or the shop that you were referring to before?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: This was the entrance to the shop, and it had a shop window, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I wish to tender those particular clips into evidence. They're already part of P78. Do Your Honours wish them tendered separately or to be identified as part of the -- part of the earlier exhibit? We've prepared two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You have these as a separate piece of film, do you?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: We've cut them and we can submit them separately. Not right at this second, but we can certainly submit the two portions which have been identified separately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that -- given our practice, that should have a separate exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: May it please the Court.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours -- Your Honours, the first clip could be Exhibit P87, and the second clip P88.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I also wish to show you a map of Dubrovnik. It's a copy of P13. Mrs. Ogresta, if you look to your left -- just turn to your left.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Uh-huh.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I want you to mark on that map. I want you to draw a square. What -- what colour is that one?

utterances.speaker: MR. USHER
utterances.text: Blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where your house was on the corner of Od Sigurate and Stradun.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've drawn a little X. Could you just make it a little more large and distinct for the exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Is that quite clear with blue or would Your Honours prefer a red or green or something bolder?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It seems quite clear at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mrs. Ogresta, could you just put some lines around it like as in a square, around the X.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. And can you also just write your name at the bottom and sign it and write the date on it. And the date is the 3rd of March.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Might that be tendered into evidence?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be P89, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm going to show you some -- another document, Ms. Ogresta. It's a portion of a report. That's MFI 51, which is known as the institute report. I'm showing the witness ERN numbers 01069448 through to 01069458. I just want you to have a look at the document. It's a report. Just have a look at the front page and the next page which is a summary followed by a number of photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And Your Honours will note there's a translation at the back of this bundle of papers. The last three pages of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: So if you could just take a moment to read that to yourself, Mrs. Ogresta.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: On the main front, the front of the building, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want you to read --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: -- read the first page and the second page.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Croatian, mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Just to yourself. Not out loud.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [In English] Excuse me. [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Going to the first photograph -- I withdraw that. The report describes some damage to a house at Od Sigurate 2. The question is simply this: Is this referring to your palace? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Turn to the photograph -- the first --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Re, I'm sorry to interrupt you, but I wonder as you're about to undertake what I think may be something that will take a little time, we might have the morning break, the first of them, now before going through the photographs. We will have a break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Turning to the first photograph, that's photograph 24, 01069450 is the number on the top. Is that a photograph depicting damage to your house or palace from -- on the Stradun side?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, that is what can be seen. Please look at the door frame. It burned down completely. And also the wall going from the ground floor to the first floor around this stone wreath. All of that burned down. And you can see that the walls are still there, but the entire interior burned down. The windows are cracked and burned, as far as I can see. And that's the way I saw it myself as a layman.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And does this show the damage that you saw to your house on the 7th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. What is written here is correct. Of course, they use expert terms so I wouldn't be competent to discuss that because I'm not an architect by training, so I wouldn't go into all of that right now, but this is the way I remember it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Earlier in your evidence you referred to, I think, being in the street and seeing what I think you described as a missile going through a window. Just go back for a moment to that.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You were then in Od Sigurate Street. That's around the corner from what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And when you looked at the --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you looked at the video which is Exhibit -- was it 88?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Exhibit 87, a still of that same shot of the house, you said you thought a missile went through that window. When you were saying that, was it something you actually saw or was it an assumption?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you were standing in -- around the corner in Od Sigurate Street. So when you --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't see it. No, I really didn't see that. But from the west side, yes, I saw that. It whizzed by and I heard this detonation and it was set to fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You said you were standing in Od Sigurate Street when your house was hit by an incendiary shell. Did you see something go through a window on the Od Sigurate side?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did see something, something flying. I don't know. I heard a detonation, and I heard something whiz by. As for the details, I really couldn't tell you about that. And then it was on fire. So I assumed that it was this incendiary, guided missile.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you look up when you heard something?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, I did look up, and I saw the house on fire. First it was the curtain that was on fire, and then everything caught fire all the way down to the bottom. It burned down very fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you is, was it the sound of the detonation, as you described it, to look up and see that your house was on fire?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what sort of time period are we talking about between you hearing this noise and seeing your house on fire?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Soon after the noise and the whizzing sound, very soon. I think that they said that something was not activated. I didn't see that, but that is what I heard from other people, that there were such kinds as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm just wanting you to tell the Trial Chamber is the conclusion you have drawn on what went into your house, is that based on an assumption and things that other people told you rather than what you actually saw yourself?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that the lady on several occasions said very decidedly what it was that she saw, before the break and now. I can even give you the exact lines. I don't see what Mr. Re is trying to do now. The lady said what she saw, and I think that we should all be grateful to her for that, rather than try now in the examination-in-chief to relativise [sic] what the lady said. So I object to this line of questioning by Mr. Re at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Re, as I understand it, you're trying to get clear whether the witness is speaking from personal observation or from an inference based on partly what she saw and partly what she was told.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's the position, Mr. Petrovic. I think it would be proper to allow the questioning. It's merely trying to make clear whether she really did see what she described or whether she's just reached that conclusion from what others may have said together with what she saw. So carry on, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Ms. Ogresta, do you understand what I'm asking you? What I'm asking you is -- the first part is, do you understand what I'm asking you? I'm asking you whether when you say you saw something go into your window and you described it as a missile and -- is that based upon what you saw, heard, and what other people have told you?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I saw something fly in, and I heard a detonation, and after that, the fire started. What it was exactly, I don't know, but it was obviously something that had set our house on fire. That I did see.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Move to the next photograph which is number 25, 01069451. What is that a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: My street from the west side, the entrance. This is the entrance, and this little window is where we had sought shelter, where we hid. You see all the rocks out here. Everything was destroyed. All of it crumbled from the top to the bottom.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just put the photograph on the ELMO to your left. The usher will assist you. And I just want you to get a pen, one that will show up on the -- on the black, and circle the window. Do a large circle around the window.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just to make it a bit clearer, could you draw an arrow from the left-hand side of the page pointing towards where the window -- where your circle is. Can you do it right from the left-hand side where the -- which is clear, please. Just a straight line right from the white part on the left-hand side of the page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters cannot hear the witness. We're sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, is that the doorway to your house?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, this is the doorway.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've just drawn a cross on the doorway. You can see --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [In English] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What is it you can see spilling out into the street from the doorway?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This -- this is debris, rocks due to the destruction, of course. First there was destruction and then there was fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does this photograph accurately depict what you saw when you returned on the 7th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. That's how we left in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Turn now to the next photograph which is number 26, ERN 01069452. It seems to be a photograph taken looking upwards. What is that a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [In English] Stradun. Od Sigurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You've just drawn on the left-hand side of the page "Od Sigurate," and on the bottom of the page "Stradun."

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You indicate that the part of the building which is on the left-hand side is in Od Sigurate and the part which is --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... on Stradun. Now, is that a photograph of your building?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And does it accurately depict the inside of your building as you saw it on the 7th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, identical to this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please turn to the next photograph which is photo number 27, number 01069453.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: What can be seen is the stone shelves with the ornaments. And we see the cracks between the second and the third levels of the building, also the stairs leading to our floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The stone shelves which you've just indicated as in the centre of the photograph, centre at the top of the photograph, were they the ones you were describing earlier this morning of the in-built shelving?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. There was another set like that on my floor, and this is between the second and the third level. It was close to the stairs, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Please turn to the next photograph which is photograph number 28, 0169 -- sorry, 01069454. This appears to be another copy of photograph 26?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: The same.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: As photograph 26. Turn now to photograph number 29. That's 01069455.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What can you tell the Trial Chamber about that photo which appears to be the interior of a burnt out building?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. The right-hand side is Od Sigurate Street and the left-hand side is the Stradun side, as far as I can see. Again, the interior which was destroyed, razed to the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And you've written on the left-hand side above the corner of the building "Stradun," and on the right-hand side above the building "Od Sigurate." I'm saying that for the record.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you look through the two windows on the right-hand side of the photograph -- just turn to the -- if you just turn to the --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. You have it there. What can you see through those two windows?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: You mean on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On the right-hand side of the photo there's two large windows below the cornices. Yes. That's where --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: That's the warehouse. That's the ground floor. That must be the door. Probably the door, the door leading to this warehouse, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Turn --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Not the warehouse that was in our building but next door.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Next door? Can you see Od Sigurate Street through those windows?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, yes, yes, yes. Our windows, we had about six of them facing Od Sigurate, Od Sigurate number 2. Imagine, I don't even know how many there were any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Turn to the next photograph, photograph 30. That's 01069456. Do you know what that is a photograph of?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Of course this is the interior but from the north, somewhere from the north. So one of the neighbours. So it's the interior, too, further on from our building.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can I just take you back. I neglected to ask you in photograph 29. Did that accurately depict the damage to the interior of your palace as you saw it on the 7th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Identical to this photograph as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Turn now to photograph number 31, 01069457.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: That's it. That's it. It's like a build-in cupboard. Destroyed, burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you just go book to photograph 27. Is that -- is photograph 31 an enlargement of the stone shelving shown in photograph 27?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, please turn to photograph 32. A moment ago I took you to photograph 29. If you could look at 29 and 32 together. 32 appears to be a more wide-angled shot of photograph 29. And photograph 32 is 01069458.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Looking at photograph 32 can you see all three floors without the loft in your building there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. The ground floor -- no. One, two. I see only two. I see only two here.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. What about at the bottom? The levels, not the floor, the levels.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: The levels. Yes. Yes. The loft isn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And again, does this photograph accurately depict what you saw when you returned to your house on the 7th of December, 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: That's what it looked like. And even worse, perhaps, in my eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you returned, there had been a fire the day before. Was the fire still burning or smouldering?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No. It was no longer burning. No smoke could be seen either.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I want you to turn now to the description at the -- on the front page of the report. In Croatian, please, the front page. I want you to go to the part that says, "Description of damage." And it says, I'm reading the English translation: "Completely gutted building with burnt and demolished roof and all floors." Does that accurately depict what you saw on the 7th of December when you came back to your house?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, it is accurately except for these details. I mean, I really don't know how to say that. The roof --

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mrs. Ogresta, I'm only talking about that line. We'll do if --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, yes. This is correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Mrs. Ogresta was giving an answer and she was interrupted. I would kindly ask that Mrs. Ogresta be allowed to finish her answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said a few minutes ago that I'm not competent to use expert terms, but as far as I can see, yes, this is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm doing it line by line for my learned friend's benefit, and also of course clarify anything like that as we go. Turn to the next part. Main -- the heading says -- is "Facade or fronts of the building." It says: "Main front due to high temperature completely burnt out and cracked door frames (number 46 and 47 on the chart.)" Did you see completely burnt and cracked door frames?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, I did see that. I think I've already said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next part says: "Completely carbonised stones in the ground-floor wall (up to the cornice between the ground floor and the first floor)." What can you say about that, the completely carbonised stones in the ground-floor wall?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It was all black. You can see it on the photographs for yourselves. Totally charred. The door, too, and the door frame, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next sentence is: "Also torched and broken window frames." It's got "mullions" in -- with a question mark, "on the 1st and 2nd floors, west side of the front." Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. That is accurate, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next line is: "Carbonised and partially broken stone roof cornice and the supporting corbels." Is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The following line says: "Vertical crack in front wall, extending from the transom above the west window on the 1st floor, along the right-hand pin of the 2nd floor window and up to the roof cornice." Now, earlier in your evidence you described a crack to the front wall. Is what is described in that, in that line there accord with what you saw when you returned on the 7th of December?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. On the west side of the house and on the south side of the house, the identical vertical crack. I think I said that even before this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Going to the next line: "West front - also carbonised and cracked window frames, mullions, and the entire stone roof gutter above this front." Again, does that accurately reflect what you saw when you returned on the 7th of December?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The next line: "Both entrance doors to the ground floor show traces of fire." Did you see that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Next: "A vertical crack at the south end of this front extending from the ground floor, along the 1st and 2nd floor windows up to the roof cornice. Identical cracks extend along the south-end windows on this front." Likewise, same question, does that accurately reflect the damage, the cracking damage you saw when you returned on the 7th of December?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Correct. Absolutely correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Now, Ms. Ogresta, I'll come back to the document a little bit later. I'm now going to ask you about the military presence, if any, in the Old Town in October, November, and December 1991. You've told the Trial Chamber that you lived in the Old Town throughout that period. Were you aware of any military installations, fortifications, or armaments in the Old Town in that period?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. There was nothing in the Old Town, no soldiers, no weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Were you aware of the protected status under UNESCO of the Old Town in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you see anything around the Old Town to indicate that it had this UNESCO protected status?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you ever see any flags?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did. On the ramparts and on St. Ivan. I think there was a blue flag with something white on it, a blue flag.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What effect, if any, did the fact of UNESCO protection have on the people of Dubrovnik and the Old Town? What did they feel or think about it?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, we felt safe.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I've showed you some photographs from what we call the institute report. Were any photographs taken on the day when your house was burning?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, the very same day the late Miroslav Kelner photographed the burning house.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have you seen those photographs?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, I have. They were displayed at an exhibition in Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Where are those photographs now?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Probably his mother has them or the late Miroslav Kelner's wife. And I assume -- well, I don't know. Perhaps some friends have several copies. I don't have any, but I saw the exhibition. Of course you can access the photographs if you need them.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Have you or your husband made any attempts to find these photographs to bring them to court?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, my husband did try, did attempt to find them, and I think he did get them. If I need to bring them in, there is probably a way in which that could be done, brought into this Honourable Tribunal. I don't know what the ways and means are.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The only other thing with this witness's evidence, Your Honours, is I move to tender this extract of the institute report MFI P51 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence, with pleasure, can observe that Mr. Re, in a satisfactory manner, demonstrated the -- an approach as to how a damage can be established with relation to certain buildings mentioned in the report P51. He did that in a very efficacious way, and he moved the witness through the damage and in a very satisfactory way created the foundations for the document he wishes to tender.
