All the Defence can do at this point is to encourage this kind of attitude and approach and to say that with respect to this particular exhibit which is being tendered, the Defence has no objections to it being admitted into evidence. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that would be Exhibit P90.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is there any cross-examination, Mr. Petrovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course, Your Honour, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mrs. Ogresta. I am lawyer Vladimir Petrovic, Defence counsel for General Strugar, and with your permission, I should like to ask you several questions with respect to the testimony here before Their Honours today.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, first of all what your profession is.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I am a pensioner and have an invalidity pension, disabled pension.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As we're speaking the same language, would you pause between question and answer to give the interpreters a chance to translate what we're saying.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, no problem there. I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me what did you do before you retired? What kind of work did you do?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I was an administrator, a medical administrator or, rather, an administrator in the health service.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What schooling have you had?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I graduated from secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us exactly where you were working in October 1991, October 1991. As far as I understood it, you were working in the health centre. So where did you go from there? Just slowly, please. Take it slowly.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, I worked at the health centre in the microbiology laboratory, and when the war broke out, we moved to Medarevo because there was a better shelter there. It was a new building, but it hadn't been completely -- it wasn't completely operational. But from the old hospital, as we all belong to the same company, we helped transfer it, transfer the patients, and although I'm not a nurse myself, I did help in the transport of patients to Medarevo which was a more secure area rather than the old hospital. And then I worked at Medarevo and later returned to the health centre itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to try and simplify this and you just tell me if I'm right or not. The health centre that you worked in, was that located in the building of the old hospital at Boninovo?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Within that compound, not in that very building but nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So that means that the health centre was in the compound of the old hospital; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, very close by.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, if I remember well, that means that it's the part of town where the old hospital was, the park called Gradac, and the Old Town; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In fact, if we take the old hospital, although we haven't got a map in front of us, the park surrounding the old hospital is the park that we called Gradac; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, no. It is before Gradac park. That's where the old hospital is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it's nearby.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It's fairly nearby. Not right next to it but fairly nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Now, the building of the new hospital, where is that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It's at Lapad called Medarevo. It is the St. Blaise hospital which takes its name after the patron saint of Dubrovnik, St. Blaise.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mrs. Ogresta, when and how did you come into contact with the OTP investigators?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Quite by chance. After the 6th of December, 1991, I lost my home, my identity. I had to go to a hotel, and I moved between 14 hotels and 50 hotel rooms. And I ended up in the hotel that was called Vis 2, and that's how I came into contact with them. We had a conversation, an informal talk, and I decided to be a witness, to come forward as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand everything you told us here today in court, but for the purposes of this Honourable Trial Chamber, would you try and focus on my questions and ask me [as interpreted] what I'm asking you. So my question was this: How did you come into contact with the gentlemen from the investigating department? Did you look them out? Did they look you out? What happened?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Through force of circumstance. The gentlemen from the Tribunal came to the hotel, and we had an interview. That was, I think, in 1999 or perhaps the year 2000. I really can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did they ask for you specifically?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No. We were refugees in the hotel, displaced persons, and it was normal for us to tell our stories, our truths, something that we had all experienced.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Tell me, please, first did you tell the investigator everything you considered to be relevant and important with respect to what happened to you in those months of 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, I did for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you tell him the most important points and things?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, the most important things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And you did your best not to omit any of the important points?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I did my best as far as I was able to, because a lot of time has gone by since then.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, of what happened on the 1st of October. What exactly did you see and where did you see it from? Just briefly.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: The 1st of October, when I got up I heard shells, explosions, but that was a little further away, not very near to the town. And then this intensified, and I thought that the dustmen were sweeping the streets, but I looked out of the window and it wasn't that. The sirens sounded. There was general confusion, people going hither and thither. That's what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's what you heard. What did you actually see?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I heard. I saw a plane shelling Srdj. I could see that from the health centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what bombs were used to attack Srdj, the transmitter?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Probably cluster bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, madam, how do you know what cluster bombs are? Have you had any experience with them? Have you ever become acquainted with cluster bombs? How come you know what a cluster bomb is?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: That's what I assumed. I heard they were cluster bombs, although I'm not well-versed in terminology of that kind, and that's a good thing because it's terrible for the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I assume you never saw the likes ever before in your life.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. I saw a shell and shrapnel on the street for the first time then. I'd never seen anything like that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, tell me then, please, how did you assume that it was this particular type of bomb, a cluster bomb?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, we were in a group when we looked at all this going on, and people would talk, and I assume someone knew. Of all my friends there, someone must have known, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I should now like to focus on what you were actually able to see from your own house. Today you told us that you had windows looking onto two sides, if I understood you correctly.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That means your windows, the windows of your apartment face the Stradun on one side. That is to say they were south facing. And you also said that on the other side your windows looked out onto the west. They were west facing and looked onto the Od Sigurate Street; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me now, please, how then were you able to see from these windows of yours, the Stradun-facing windows, how were you able to see Srdj, Mount Srdj from those windows?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Because I have a loft, and you can see Srdj wonderfully well up there. You couldn't see the loft on the photograph because it was burnt down, but you could see the Imperijal Hotel and everything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, what about the loft windows? Where were they facing?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: You can see. They are between the roof and the next-door roof. There was a window there, and you could see everything from it. Well, it's the second street from the cloister, the Mala Braca cloister. Have you been to Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I would like you to tell me the following: Is Mount Srdj to the north of the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So how, then, from south-facing windows were you able to see something that was behind your back?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I wasn't looking southwards. I looked westwards. If I turn my head I can see Mount Srdj from the window. I can take you there to the Dubrovnik. They've reconstructed the facade of the building now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So from that south-facing window you were able to see Mount Srdj which was to the north?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: If you were looking to the west you could see Srdj, which was to the north. It's a small window in the loft area with a small terrace.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to be very specific in asking my questions.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: And I'm being very specific in answering your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Today, on page 7, line 18 of the transcript, you described what you could see from your windows, the windows looking out onto the Stradun, and there you stated that: "I always looked at Srdj from the windows facing the Stradun side." You didn't mention any west-facing windows. You just mentioned the south-facing windows. Is that what you said?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't think that's what I said. I really do think that I don't mention -- that I didn't mention the south-facing windows but the west view. Check it out, because I couldn't say something that actually wasn't the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's what it says, and my colleague Mr. Re would have put me right had I quoted you wrongly. But never mind. It's not important. Let's move on. Tell me, please, your building, it was a valuable building, wasn't it? What was protected on that building? Did I understand you correctly that your building enjoyed external protection and that it was protected and enjoyed protection both on the facade, the exterior, and the interior? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As far as I was able to understand, as regards of the interior of the building, you did some serious renovation and interventions there. Did you have permits to go ahead with this construction work from the Dubrovnik cultural institute?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. We didn't knock down anything that was old. We just made it more beautiful.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So on the 1st of October, you saw from your apartment as shells were falling on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, not on the 1st of October. I only heard detonations. On the 1st of October, town -- war started in town. When the first siren went off, I did not see that. It was on the 6th of December that I saw that, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. What was on Srdj? Why were they bombing Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about what was on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you perhaps see shooting from Srdj ever?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I never saw any such thing. I just saw shells falling on Srdj. As for shooting, I never saw that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know that the Croatian army was at the Imperijal Fort on Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that. I didn't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Have you ever heard of any such thing?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: As for the town of Dubrovnik, I mean Gruz, Lapad, Ploce, St. Jakov, were there any Croatian troops there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I didn't see that. I don't know. I can say that in town there weren't any, and as for out of town, I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you go to work every day?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Every day. And I was afraid as to when I'd come [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Chamber where you went.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I went round the corner but always from Zarkovica. They targeted us with snipers and machine-guns. They were really taking it out on us. It was hard for us to walk that way. Only sometimes a vehicle from the hospital would come and pick us up, but I would usually walk. We would usually walk. It was really bad, really, really bad.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Again, I'm asking you to answer my question. If you went on foot, which streets did you take?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I went towards the west via Pile Gate, then I went out to Pile, then the street formerly called Marshala Tita [as interpreted], and then Gradac, the old hospital, the medical centre, and then I'd turn left and that's where the new hospital of Medarevo is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: This street of Marshal Tito, is it now called the street of Ante Starcevic?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think so. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And you took that same route every day and went back the same way?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: For the most part. Sometimes I'd stay on at the hospital, although the hospital was shelled too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Can I please ask you to focus on my questions. Whatever my colleague wanted to ask you he did ask you, so there is no -- and you answered those questions and we will finish sooner if you just answer my questions.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So the route you took every day, on this route did you ever see an armed person or a person in uniform?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: During the three months that we're talking about, October, November, and December, did you ever see on this route that we are referring to a Croatian soldier or a Croatian policeman?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Generally speaking, in the town of Dubrovnik, not taking into account the Old Town, were there any Croatian soldiers or Croatian police there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I cannot say whether they were there or not. I didn't see any of them. In town there certainly weren't any. And outside the town, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: For the Trial Chamber, could you please make sure that we make a distinction. When we say the Old Town, then we mean the Old Town. When we say the town of Dubrovnik, then we mean Lapad, Gruz, Ploce, everything that is part of town; right? So that it would be clear to all. First and foremost, the distinguished Trial Chamber. So throughout this time, you didn't see anyone. Now, tell me, did you perhaps hear of the presence of Croatian police or army in the town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters ask could the witness's microphone please be turned on, the other one as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Have you perhaps heard of the term the "Defenders of Dubrovnik"?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, later, much later.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Who were these people who were called the defenders of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Who they were? Those who defended it probably. If they are defenders, they -- they were defending their homeland from the enemy, probably those who came by force and tried to enter by force. But we did not set anything on fire, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you know any of the defenders of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Did I know any? Yes. Yes, I did know one. I knew a friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to give us his name?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I've almost forgotten. Zeljko is his first name, and the last name -- he's deceased. He got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know when he was killed and under what circumstances?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I really don't know. I think he was in the Civil Defence, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in this period October, November, December?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Once but in civilian clothes, from the window, before this 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You saw him from the window of your house, I assume, the one that faces --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Stradun.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when was he killed approximately, at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think it was somewhere around the beginning. I don't know. I don't know exactly. I cannot say exactly. Putica, Zeljko, Putica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you say the beginning, you're probably referring to the month of October, November?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, because in December our house burnt down, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, when you saw him then, did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. I was at the window and he just waved his hand at me for the very last time in his life.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see whether he had been armed?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No. He was wearing civilian clothes. He was there with other people strolling down Stradun.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you know any of the people who were with him?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me -- tell me, did you know anything about where he was, what he did? You say that he was in this Civil Defence. Did you know anything about where he was?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: He worked at the waterworks. I really don't know how come he ended up in the Civil Defence. But, look, I mean if a war broke out, of course he had to prepare in this way, but he was not attached to the military, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was there any mobilisation in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. As far as I know, no. My nephew was 33 then, approximately, but he was not called up. He was not mobilised at all. My husband, whom I met later on, had not been mobilised either. I don't know about anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether anybody else had been mobilised?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know. No one in my street was mobilised, no one.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear about this at all?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to tell us why you said then to the investigator Mohammed Arshad in June 2000 why you said to him what you're denying now, and this is what you said: "I heard that the Croats when the conflict started were mobilised to fight against the enemy forces." That is what you stated to him then?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I really did not hear that. I have no idea. It's been such a long time really.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you not tell him this or did you forget that you told him about this?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. I have no idea. I really don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: He probably added this on his own, then?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, I don't think so. No. I'm just saying I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps forget this fact, then? Have you forgotten since 2000?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, yes, but perhaps I didn't attach any importance to it. It's only natural that there had to be a defence. None of my people were there, so then perhaps I just forgot about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, what was it that people had to defend themselves with? Did they have any weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Nothing. How could they get weapons? And our army that we had financed and paid for so handsomely had turned their weapons on us. They started killing us with those same weapons that we paid for.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the positions of the defenders were?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were there any at all?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. I wasn't interested in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, did you perhaps ever see any man in uniform, an ordinary policeman anywhere in town?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: An ordinary policeman?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In the town of Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I didn't. Only when we'd walk on Porporela, then I'd hear some music from Zarkovica, some kind of folk music. So you see, I guess it was not our troops up there. Perhaps the army that we had had before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see an ordinary policeman at the Pile Gate?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No. Not that either. Perhaps there was one, but I would try to hide as much as I could, and I would be glancing at the hill up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, was anybody maintaining law and order in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. We were at home all the time. We were -- we did not go to the shelter, and what the Civil Defence did is something I really don't know about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you were at Porporela, did you see these soldiers at Zarkovica?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but they weren't that nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you perhaps remember the uniforms, the colour of the uniforms?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Greenish. I have no idea.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember perhaps whether a cannon could be seen there or a tank or something? Did you see anything at Zarkovica from Porporela?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see whether they had any weapons?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think they had a machine-gun, a machine-gun in their hands. And every evening, I can tell you that, when we would have dinner in the loft, they would target our window every evening and shrapnel fell in then too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that. Tell me, from Porporela to Zarkovica --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: -- how far is that as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, how much -- well, it's very nearby, because these soldiers got even closer, all the way down to Ploce, you know, that part. They were so close. Their positions were probably at Zarkovica. I have no idea. At any rate, I saw them and I heard this folk music, and then I assumed that that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did they enter the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No. No, they did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: If they came to Ploce --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, not exactly to Ploce but below Zarkovica. Very nearby. So we saw them from Porporela. And one day a gentleman walked in front of me and a sniper hit him. He lives near St. Marija. His last name is Saric. What his first name is I have no idea. But he was injured, he was wounded by a sniper.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you be so kind as to tell us the following: This place where you saw them, below Zarkovica and then to Porporela there's about a couple of hundred metres; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: 250, 300 metres?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, sort of, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, do you know why these people from Zarkovica or, rather, from below Zarkovica did not enter town?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Ask them. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there perhaps someone or something between Zarkovica and town?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, no one as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, where were you watching from and from where could you see that there was no one there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I didn't see anybody else except for them.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there someone perhaps at the houses or hotels who was stopping these people from Zarkovica from getting closer?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know. I cannot talk about things I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please, when you were moving about and you said that for three months you went to work and back all the time, did you ever see an armoured vehicle moving about?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No, I really didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you perhaps see an armoured vehicle ever bringing in the wounded to hospital?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, I did not. I worked in the administration, so I didn't actually have any contact with the patients.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear anything about that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I heard that there were wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear that APCs brought in the wounded?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat what was damaged on the 1st of October?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: The 1st of October, all the damages?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I mean in the Old Town.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: The Rupe museum, I think the Sponza building was damaged too, as well as the cloister of Mala Braca. And then later on --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking you about the 1st of October.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I can't say exactly because a lot of time has gone by. I don't know the exact dates and what happened when, but I do know what was hit. Ploce, that's outside the Old Town --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's take this step by step slowly, please. Let's summarise what your testimony was as you told my learned colleague, and now you can tell me. On the 1st of October it was Sponza, Sveti Vlaho, St. Blaise, and Mala Brace, the cloister?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: And the Rupe museum too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Right, the Rupe museum too.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Whether that was October or November, I can't really be specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You mean just as regards the Rupe museum?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. I mean everything in actual fact. I assume that's the month it happened, because from the 1st of October, there was constant bombing or shelling, almost every day. So I really can't remember those details. I really can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: From the 1st of October, was this on a daily basis or was the Old Town shelled almost every day?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, not each and every day but almost every day, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, were there some days when there was no shelling?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, yes, that did happen. There could have been a lull for a couple of days, but -- and really I found it very strange when there wasn't an explosion at night when I was about to go to sleep. And we had no electricity, so it would light up the room when there was an explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You couldn't go to sleep if you didn't hear the sound of a shell exploding?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Then there was something out of ordinary, by means that there was continuous shelling. It was unusual for me to not hear those terrible explosions every night.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So that means you would hear those explosions. And where did you sleep, in the loft?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, I slept downstairs on the second floor. I could hear -- I was too much of an optimist.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you went to sleep with all these explosions, and then you would -- you didn't go to the shelter?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. Only when it was the worst situation, for the couple of worst days.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When there was no explosion?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, then I would go around walking, walk around.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, why did you never go to a shelter?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I had a phobia of shelters. There were too many people in too small a space. It was claustrophobic. I didn't like going.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever enter a shelter?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, one night we slept in the shelter of the Park Hotel on a wooden table. That's the only day throughout the war that I spent in a shelter.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But all that came later, after the 6th of December.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, and after the 6th of December, I didn't go to the shelter. I went to my neighbour's and took shelter there because the building was built up more.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When you said that on the 1st of October you looked through the window and saw nobody out in the streets --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Not nobody anywhere. I meant --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you allow me to finish my question.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, let me ask my question first and then you can answer. Don't interrupt, please. You said that on the 1st of October, you looked out of your window and that you saw nobody anywhere on the Stradun. That's what you told us. When was that? When did you look out the window and where were the people, if you happen to know?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I looked out of the window in the morning. I looked through the window when I heard the explosion. I thought it was the dustmen banging about with their bins, but it wasn't the dustmen, and then I realised what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And the people, all the people who are usually out on the Stradun?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It was morning. It wasn't summertime to have people out in the streets that early.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, your own house, you said it was very close to Srdj. What do you mean by very close? How close is very close?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, as the crow flies, I don't know how many metres it would be, but it's close by.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: It's even closer than Zarkovica is to Porporela; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, roughly speaking, yes. Zarkovica is a little towards this end. But there is a fortress up on Mount Srdj so I couldn't see anybody.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I only asked you how far it was. I know you didn't see anybody. I understand that. What I'm interested in is the distance, how far it is. So several hundred metres would you say?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. I assume that's the distance. I felt that they would come into town from Zarkovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see any flags up on Mount Srdj?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, when you look towards Srdj --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: -- how many times did you see these explosions at Srdj? Was this on a daily basis, every day?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, let me think. No, it wasn't every day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, how many times did you see that happen, roughly?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: How many times? That's a tough question. I really can't say. On the 6th of December, I saw one, and before that when the Imperijal Hotel was set fire to. So three or four times.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you saw that up at Srdj three or four times.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: While I was at home.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you just wait to hear my question, please, once again. As I was saying, you saw that three or four times, whereas the Old Town was almost targeted every day except for a few exceptions. Am I right in saying that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, do you know what a guided missile is?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose there's a code and it knows where to land. "Guided" means that; right? Guided to the target. But of course I'm not competent enough to be able to speak about those military matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, why, when the investigator talked to you, did you not mention a guided missile at all? You never mentioned anything like that.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I really don't know. It's just come to my mind now, because you know, a lot of time has gone by and now I've sort of begun to unwind the tape and remember things that I didn't previously remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, Mrs. Ogresta, you gave a very detailed statement. You speak about many things that we have heard here in the courtroom today, but you did not make a single mention of that guided missile at all.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Perhaps I used the term the first time today. I don't know. Perhaps I did previously. I don't remember what I told the investigator. I really don't. It's just come to me now. I suddenly thought of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When did it come to you?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Just now, this particular moment. I realised that this was the term, "guided."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure the investigator didn't ask you about that or did he, how your house was hit?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, yes, he did ask me, but I don't know. My brain cells, grey matter seems to have unraveled it all now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to tell you -- read out, in fact, what you told him, and I'll limit myself to the important part. "I cannot tell you the exact number of shells that fell on our palace, nor can I say anything about the number shells which did not explode. I also cannot say much about the types of shells because I don't know anything about that."

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, and now suddenly --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Would you wait for me to ask the question, my question, please. In the year 2000 you knew nothing about the types of shells or at least that's what you told Mr. Arshad, the investigator. So how come you've just remembered guided missiles and the rest of the things you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. By process of association, I suppose. It's just come to my mind, guided missiles, that the shells were guided. Why, I don't know. I can ask God how I came to that. I don't know. God only knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, as you knew nothing about that, and you are quite explicit on that point, how come that in the meantime you learnt something about it? Did you talk to anybody? Did you consult anybody?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No, I did not. Perhaps I heard of it. I really don't know. I can't say anything about the profile of the shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, would you please be so kind as to tell me when you saw the photographs that we showed in the courtroom a moment ago, did you happen to look at them a couple of days ago, a few days ago?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, I didn't see them, but I remembered them very well. That image will always stay with me throughout my life, for as long as I live.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, did you -- have you talked to anybody since you've been here in The Hague?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. Who do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You didn't talk to anybody?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. Who do you mean? Talk to who? Do you mean professionally, privately? What do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I mean did you talk to, for example, someone from the witness and victims unit, for example?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you talk to anybody from the Prosecution, the OTP?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, why did you say a moment ago that you didn't talk to anybody?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I didn't know who you had in mind. Did you talk to any Defence counsel? That would be normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you did talk to somebody from the OTP?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, for goodness sake, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, why didn't you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I didn't think it was important. I thought that was the general procedure, that you had to talk to somebody. I didn't attach any importance to it, because nobody can tell me what the truth was if I didn't experience it myself. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I completely agree with that. That's normal.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I've told you everything now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So what did you discuss?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, nothing. Where I am now, what I'm doing now, how it all happened, that kind of thing. I told them my life story or, rather, my tragedy, my personal tragedy as experienced by me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you discuss the 6th of December?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, we did discuss the 6th of December, and how. And I described it like I'm describing it to you all, as I described it a moment ago to Their Honours, before the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were you perhaps shown your statement, the one you gave in the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I didn't pay any attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did they show you the statement you gave in the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I didn't look at it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Re show you your statement or not?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: He showed it to me, but I didn't read it, to tell you the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And why did Mr. Re show you your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Just like that. No reason. Did you show your witnesses their statements? Do you show your witnesses their statements?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Re show you anything else apart from your statement?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So he showed you your statement and you didn't pay any attention to it?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, not even -- not the least bit. It was on the table in front of him. I didn't pay attention to it. And I thought that that was done with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, did he ask you whether what you had written in your statement was correct and true?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what did you tell him?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: That it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you take a look at the statement before that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, just glanced at it. Is it not true and correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Re read the statement out to you?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, he did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And he didn't give you the statement to read?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I just glanced through it and said it was all right. Why should I look at it? I assume if you tell the truth, then you don't have to read through it. I couldn't say something that wasn't true. It was what had happened to me. So that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When Mr. Re had you -- you had been shown the statement by Mr. Re, you would have seen there was nothing in the statement with respect to guided missiles or guide shells.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, that doesn't matter. I've just started to unwind the whole film since I've been here in The Hague. I tried to put it to rest, to forget about it, but I can't forget. I still feel that I'm in the hotel now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So Mr. Re didn't show you the photographs and the text that you read out a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: He didn't?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, did you happen to remember guide missiles when you read it in the text?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, it was a process of association. I don't know. I don't know how that detail came to mind. Perhaps something rang a bell or by process of association brought me to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps you thought of it when you read it through.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, a red light went on, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, did you ever talk to anybody about the damage that your house incurred in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I understood that the whole house had burnt down. So what do you mean destroyed, destruction? It was fifth category. It was completely burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did anybody come to talk to you from the institute for the protection of cultural monuments, for example, or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, they did not communicate with us because we weren't the proprietors. We just had tenant's rights, so they just spoke to the owners.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So they didn't come to see you or your sister to ask you anything about how it all happened?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No, they didn't. We went there to establish the category. We went to the Institute for Reconstruction and Development to have them come out on the spot and to put our building into one of the categories that they had established for damaged buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: At the beginning or, rather, after the 6th of December, quite soon afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, please, on that occasion, did they ask you how the damage was used, what happened, how it all happened?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. I assumed they knew. They saw that the building had been burnt down. I assumed they knew that it had been hit, that we didn't burn the tyres at all. When I heard that, well, you know how I felt.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So they didn't ask you anything about the exploded or unexploded shells? They didn't ask you anything about that, none of that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, they didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, as you say, you'd forgotten. They didn't ask you about guided missiles, not guided missiles, mortar shells, anything like that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. How could they ask me? Why, in what way and why?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, I assume they didn't ask you anything either about the types of mortars, the projectiles, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, they did not. All they saw was that they destroyed everything. They, first of all, destroyed the house and then it was set fire to. What else is there to ask? I -- the only thing I was sorry was that I thought that I would never see my killers. I wouldn't see the person who would cause my death.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, is this a good time to break for the pause?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. We will have a 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Ogresta, you said several times that bullets coming from machine-guns had hit the windows of your house; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So these bullets from the machine-gun hit the window on the south side facing the Stradun and the west side window facing Od Sigurate.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, no. It was occasionally gunfire when the shells would stop falling. So it would hit us every now and then. How -- what's the word for this? Let me just remember. Ah, yes, I remember the word. The wooden blinds, the wooden shutters, that's where the bullets were implanted, but that was during the lull.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to tell me which shutters, which ones.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Up in the loft, way up in the loft. I told you I could see Srdj from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Is this on the south side?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: On the west side.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So on the south side nothing got into the shutters?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. I didn't notice anything. Only on the west side, from the west side, up in the loft. So it wasn't on the 6th of December only.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How many times did this happen, this coming from the west side?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: In the evening sort of. A few times. We were so frightened, we didn't go to the loft.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever find any remains?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, there were some.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, military-aged men, were they allowed to leave the town of Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, many left, as far as I can remember, men and women. But of course, most people who left were women and children. But there were quite a few men who left, too, yes. But women and children primarily had the right to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: What did your nephew do in October, November, and December 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: He did nothing. I mean, I already said, I think, that he worked at this printing press at Dubac in Zupa outside Dubrovnik. It had been hit. His company went down the drain, so he was unemployed. His name Said Dilberovic. He did not do his military service, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did he join the Croatian army later?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did he do his military service in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was he able bodied?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And nobody ever called him up into the military?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No one ever called him up into the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, where was your nephew that night between the 5th and the 6th?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: At his mother-in-law's, his mother-in-law being Mrs. Vera Gudelj at Boninovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, why did your nephew go from the apartment where he had lived all his life in the Old City? Please let me finish my question. When you all assumed it was safer in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. Boninovo is close to the Old Town and I don't think that a single shell fell there. And they had a good cellar up there. And since it was the little boy's birthday on the 30th of November, before that, I mean about ten days before that, they went there and they simply stayed on. They simply stayed on. I think it was the finger of fate. So they have a barbecue there, they have an outdoor terrace. They probably wanted to cheer the little boy up, I guess, things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So it was safer there than in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I wouldn't say that it was safer, but they have a pretty good cellar, you see, so that's the way it was. For the birthday, it was better. They could celebrate his fourth birthday better in that case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know what a Crisis Staff is?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. Probably a staff that was established at a time of crisis, either when there's a natural disaster or war or caused by natural causes or man-made. I don't know whether that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what was the role of the Crisis Staff in the war?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I really don't know. I'm not very knowledgeable about such things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was a Crisis Staff in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you listen to the radio over those months that you were in Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Those months, is that what you're asking me?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes, October, November, December 1991.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: In town, I heard the radio a bit, and I heard that we in the Old Town were burning tyres, we the Ustashas. That's what I heard. Then we could hear Radio Trebinje saying things like that. We didn't have any electricity, so we could only use battery-operated transistor radios. They were saying all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there a Radio Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, there was a Radio Dubrovnik. Of course there was, in town. But we didn't have any electricity, so those who had batteries could listen to radio programmes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And when you got batteries you only listened to Radio Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Radio Dubrovnik, too. We listened to whatever we could.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear statements of the Crisis Staff on Radio Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you hear on Radio Dubrovnik, for instance, where there would be bread, where there would be other food supplies? Did you hear things like that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, not over those three months. We bought some tinned food when the war started. We barely managed to get hold of a chicken but we didn't have much else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you have any bread over those months, October, November, December?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes we did. My sister went to get it since I went to work in the morning. Where she bought the bread I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You never bought bread during those three months?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did your sister buy bread somewhere in the Old Town?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, in the Old Town for sure. She didn't go out of town, no. It was in the Old Town for sure. She would have been too frightened to go out.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So where did she buy it?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. Believe me, I guess some shops were open. Od Puca, Miha Pracata, the marketplace, somewhere around there. Perhaps Mediator. It had just started working. Nowadays there is a chain in town, but at that time there was just this one shop. I think that it was Mediator where she went most often.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Oh, so she went there.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think there or in the Pavlovic -- well, or perhaps Mediator at the market. I don't know. Somewhere in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever go there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: When do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In October, November, December.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, never. I just went to work, and I came home and I didn't want to go out after that. Only if shelling would start, then I would go to our neighbour's together with Mrs. Marija Matic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. On the 6th of December, why did you not go to your neighbour's?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, look, I could not believe that it would be this kind of intensity. At one moment, we really could not go out. If we'd get out, we'd get killed. We had no way out of this. And then we were encouraged by our neighbour, and had he not rescued us, we would have gotten killed there for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, how many shells hit your house?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: A countless number. I don't know how many, but it was non-stop. When we were on the ground floor, it was going on non-stop above us. And I was thinking at that moment, Oh, my goodness, I'll die young. I wasn't even 40 at the time. But it would be so terrible to be killed among all the ruins and not to see the face of the man who was doing this to you. It was awful.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you say a countless number. 10, 20, 30?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't know. It went on for so long and at such intensity that I thought I'd go deaf before I died. We had really reconciled ourselves to our fate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All these shells fell on your house?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, above our heads. I thought it was hitting me in the head. We couldn't even move our arms or hands left or right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that. How many shells fell in your street altogether?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Ah, you're asking me too much. I really didn't do any counting then or do I know. I mean, honestly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Were there 20, 30, 40 there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I really don't know. From all sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So the detonations were every few seconds or minutes or how often?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It seemed to me it was very fast. I really cannot tell you anything in greater detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, these shells were falling on the houses and on the street itself?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, on the house. The window right above us.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: I'm asking you about the street.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, no, no. I didn't see any falling there except for the neighbour's roof. There was a hole in the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to clarify this for us. So let's say tens of shells fell on your house.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. And as for the other houses in the street and the street itself, just as many fell or perhaps more or less?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know how many fell in the street, directly onto the street I don't know. I know that this one shell fell on our neighbour's house, and now -- but I have the impression that there was non-stop shooting, that our house was being hit all the time. I don't know whether they were targeting the Franciscan cloister or the festival building, but at any rate, it was our house that was hit the most in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, shrapnel that flew by that you saw --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: -- was it from the shells that were falling on your house?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think so. Well, look, I assume that these were shells that were falling on our house. I think so. At any rate, we saw them at the window. We saw them as they were falling, so we couldn't move left or right. We would have been hit otherwise. Now, whether they were falling on the street or whatever, at any rate, these shells, it seemed to us were falling right above our heads, not directly on the street. That's was our impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you watch through that little window?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. But I didn't really see them on the street. I mean, we would have been killed for sure. Perhaps they fell up and then they ricochetted as far as I know about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So from this small window you saw this shrapnel flying all over the place?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I heard them. Like rain, like a torrent, and it's this strange sound.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, not a single shrapnel hit that window?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Oh, no, but had we moved just a tiny little bit, we would have been finished. Had we moved just a tiny little bit, we would have been hit for sure, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, if I saw this photograph properly -- just a moment, please. Do I infer this correctly --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last three digits are 451, Your Honours. Could I please ask to have P90 shown to the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I think it's 25, photo 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please take a look at photograph 25. I hope it's already --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it is on the monitor. It is on the monitor, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: How big is the window, one metre by one metre?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It's a tiny little window with bars. Oh, you want me to point at it here. I see. This one here, this tiny little window here. It has bars on it and we were standing --

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Just tell me how big is the window?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It's small.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: One metre by one metre?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, it's not that big. I think it's like this big. Perhaps half a metre.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't need this any longer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind as to describe this to the Trial Chamber. These shrapnel made of lead that you saw through the window, what does this look like and how does this move?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Very fast. Lead, a silvery colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So do they hit things?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It's like rain, like hail, as if this kind of rain was falling on the house. So actually, it was stronger than hail, a bit stronger than hail, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, as they were flying --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: -- what colour were they, a burning blaze, silvery, black?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: It seems to me they were burning. I really can't remember these details that well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But the important thing is that you saw them.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I did see them. And I heard them, as if it had been raining.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, how come you know that some shells did not explode, those that fell in your house?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: My sister went there with this other neighbour we have, and they saw this, and he said, "Let's go downstairs because there are some unexploded shells here." This is before the house was set on fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Oh, so on that day he saw this upstairs, these unexploded shells.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: On the first floor -- no, the second floor. The second floor. They couldn't go further up. It seemed to him that there were some. They were afraid, so that's why they went back. He was afraid that there were some shells that were not exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was he afraid because of the unexploded shells or did he see it?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I really don't know. He said he assumed there were more shells that were unexploded, and he said, "It's terrible. Let's go."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You said that the first shell hit your house at 9.00 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. It was hit earlier on. 6.00 o'clock -- or, rather, 10.00 o'clock, but it became faster, and later on the house -- well, we went downstairs and it -- just in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You said: "The first shell hit the roof of our palace at around 9.00 o'clock." You told the investigator that.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, perhaps that was right. All I know is that it started at 6.00 a.m., and we went downstairs. Now, whether it was exactly 9.00, I can't say. The shelling started, so whether it was exactly 9.00 o'clock, I can't say. I didn't have a watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So that means 9.00 o'clock, not 6.00 o'clock?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. It started straight away, quickly. When it was exactly, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Had I known I'd been asked all these details, I would have written them all down.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You say the first shell hit the roof and caused a hole?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Not on my house but in my neighbour's house. I don't know where the first shell fell. I was downstairs. All I knew was that I heard it, felt it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm asking you. You say: "At around 9.00 o'clock, the first shell hit the roof of our palace and made a hole in it." That's what you told the investigators.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't remember saying that. I know that it hit somewhere in the upper regions. I assumed it was in the roof.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you see that hole yourself?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I did when I went outside the house before it went up in flames. I saw the hole.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Where were you standing and how could you see the hole in the roof?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: While the house was being targeted, I didn't see it, I couldn't see it then. I saw it when I left the house, when I stepped outside, before it went up in flames. I saw the hole up there, and half the roof was shattered. The house was half destroyed when we left it, stepped outside. And I said that we started choking from the smoke and debris and all the rest of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You told my learned colleague today at one point that the guided missile from the west and south set fire to the curtains in your loft.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, not the loft, on the second floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Very well, the second floor. So is that true and correct?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Then you told my colleague that at that point in time, you were in front of Vladimir's house in the Od Sigurate Street number 4. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So standing outside the house that was Od Sigurate Street number 4, you were looking in the direction of your own house.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And then you saw this guided -- just let me finish, please -- and you saw this guided missile entering through the window on the second floor; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Could you kindly tell us now, please, what colour the shell or missile was that entered the second floor window?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I didn't notice the colour. I didn't see what colour it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And straight afterwards, you saw flames coming out through the window?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. That was after the destruction. First of all, it all toppled and then the flames started.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And when the shell entered through the window or, rather, this guided -- misguided, guided missile when it hit the window on the second floor of your house, and we're talking about the Od Sigurate Street house, were you there alone? Who else was there?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: A friend of mine, the neighbour, Mr. Vladimir Srhoj, my sister, the other neighbours, there were quite a lot of them. There was Mrs. Hadzimatovic, there was Mr. Cikata, there was Mr. Milan, I've forgotten his surname, Tomovic, I believe, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was actually attempting to object to the last question before it was answered. The evidence my learned friend is putting to the witness isn't quite correct because she did actually clarify in her examination-in-chief that she didn't actually quite see a guided missile go through the window but it was a conclusion she came to on the basis of seeing something and being told other things. So I ask that he put correctly to the witness if he's going to question the witness about the "guided missile".

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, I think that's correct, Mr. Petrovic. As I understood her evidence in the end she saw a projectile of some type go through the window and she saw what then followed, but she herself could not say whether it was a guided missile. She was told by somebody else that it was. But I think your question remains valid if we just change "projectile" for "guided missile."

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I'll do my best to clear that point up, to make it completely clear. Perhaps my question was a little misleading or confusing, or Mrs. Ogresta responded in a confused fashion. But let's recapitulate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Mrs. Ogresta, you stood with all the people we mentioned a moment ago in front of the building in the Od Sigurate Street number 4, and you saw a guided missile entering the window on the second floor of your palace.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, I saw a projectile. I assume it was a guide missile, and I saw it go directly into or through the window.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think things are clear now what the testimony of this witness is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Also, when we looked at the video a moment ago, the footage taken on the 7th of December, you showed us or pointed out to us on the facade of your building, looking towards the Stradun, you pointed to the left-hand window on the second floor, and you said that it was through that second-floor, left-hand window that a projectile entered as well; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I assume. That's what I heard.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So of those two projectiles which we have just described here was what caused the fire on your building?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly whether there were just two projectiles.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Let's check this slowly, step by step. So beforehand, before that time your house had been hit by many projectiles?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Before this particular time your house did not go up in flames.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, it didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Now, to make things quite clear, when you say "no," you mean it wasn't set on fire.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So when these two projectiles hit, you said that they hit the curtains and then the house was set fire to.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. At least soon afterwards it went up in flames.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me just now, please, something about the festival building, the Festival Palace. When my learned friend asked you, you said that you had the impression that the fire came up from the bottom, from the bottom up.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I really don't know. I don't remember. It was all a trauma for us. We did our best to put the fire out in my house, and then we took the water from this well, and in the meantime the Festival Palace building was set on fire. So we tried to extinguish the fire there, but that wasn't possible. It was already aflame.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But am I right in saying and in noting your response to my colleague that you said that in the festival building it was the bottom floor that was set fire to first and then the flames spread upwards?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I might have been wrong. It started at the top. We weren't able to open the door. That's why it was a problem. We weren't able to open the door to the festival building, and the fire was spreading. That was the problem. We lost time and couldn't open the door.
