Then this other man, Mr. Mladjo, opened the door and we then we attempted without success to put out the fire. I don't know that it was hit by a shell, but it was in flames very quickly. Whether the flames caught from our own house, I don't know, but it was up in flames very quickly afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: But it was set alight after your own building caught fire?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, soon afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, perhaps the fire from your building caught the festival building and spread to the Festival Palace?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't believe so. We were out in the street trying to put the fire out. There was shooting still going on, and the building was up in flames.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was there a strong wind that fanned the flames perhaps?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No. On the contrary. It was cold but still no wind.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: You told us today that the fire brigade arrived on the scene very soon after the fire broke out. How did they arrive? Did they come in a vehicle, fire engine, or what?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't know. I know that they came in a car. How many of them there were. They came in a vehicle. They tried to put out the fire but without success. And it was general chaos. Everybody came to see what was happening from all over town. They didn't seem to be afraid. They came to see what was going on.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, you don't know how many of them there were, but they came in the red fire engine, didn't they?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I suppose so. As far as I can remember. I really don't know. I think so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, a moment ago in response to my colleague's questions, you said that to all intents and purposes, all the other houses in the Od Sigurate Street were either not damaged or the damage was minor, and I'm not talking about the monastery, just in the houses in the lower part of your street, Od Sigurate Street. Just a moment, please. Let me finish. Does that mean, then, that the shells which fell were for the most part shells that fell on your own house, not any other shells, that there weren't any other shells?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: On the other building, I said that the roof to my neighbour's house was hit, the summer festival building, but I didn't see any other damage. I really didn't. There weren't any other -- there wasn't any other damage.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: In your statement you said the following, and it was a very interesting point. You say: "In the Old Town, I did not see a single cannon, sniper, or anything like that, but it is difficult to say anything about the area outside the Old Town."

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes. If I wasn't there, I couldn't say. I was in the old part of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So you didn't see anything?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Do you know who Damir Ogresta is?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Damir Ogresta? It's my brother-in-law, if that's the man. He was a sailor.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Where was he in 1991?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: In Dubrovnik. I assume he was in Dubrovnik, but I didn't -- I hadn't met my husband yet at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what part of town is your husband from?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: He's from Boninovo, opposite the health centre. Near the Boninovo cemetery, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And did you happen to hear that Mr. Damir Ogresta was a member of the Croatian police force during the material time, October, November, December?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, and I didn't know him at the time, and we're not on good terms now anyway.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you happen to hear that he was the commander of the police station in Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you happen to hear that your brother-in-law had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss the events of 1991 with your husband?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. He never told me about his brother. He didn't live with his brother, and I never even met the brother.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss the events of 1991 with your husband?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, I did, and my husband kept a diary too.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Was your husband involved in any of the units at that time?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And your husband never told you that his brother was the chief of the police station in Mokosica?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No, he didn't, and I never asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, tell me, please, you said that at the beginning of October, the damages to the Sponza Palace, St. Blaise, and so on --

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: -- tell us what the damage done was. What did it look like?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, holes. There were holes, some cracks of some sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the Sponza Palace building, where were the cracks?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Ah, you're asking me too much. I really can't say. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Well, did you see the damage?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but I didn't remember. I didn't pay that much attention. I just looked at my house and I don't, in fact, go into town any more because that brings to memory what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: On the St. Blaise church, did you see the damages?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, but there was some reconstruction there although there were some cracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: So in October, where were -- was the damage on St. Blaise church, roughly?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Probably on the roof. I don't know. You're asking me too much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: And what about the Rupe museum?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I know it was damaged too, but I didn't go there to see. People said that it had been damaged. I didn't personally go up there.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Petrovic. Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown the map she marked. I think it's Exhibit P89 or 90 -- 89.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic asked you about damage to your neighbour Mr. Vladimir Srhoj's house. I just want you to mark on the map a square with an A in the middle of it where his house is in relation to yours.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You seem to have marked on a different street.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [In English] It's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you put the mark in the middle of the street, can you please just draw onto the shaded bit where his house actually is. As in a bird's-eye view, just draw in a square.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's still on the street.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can you put an A next to it, please.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. And that's number 4, is it?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yeah. [Interpretation] Yes, number 4, I think. One, two, three, four, I think it was. One, two -- I think it was four.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: That could be returned.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Four or five. I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just like to ask that this be marked in some way, the house where the lady was, to have it identified on this map somehow, because this way it remains unclear. So I would kindly ask my colleague to take care of that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Perhaps we could do a legend on the side, an X for the witness's house and an A for Mr. Vladimir Srhoj's house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The court officer might be able to do that for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'll keep going while you do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You told Mr. Petrovic in cross-examination that you heard some folk music from some soldiers. What sort of folk music was it?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Serb folk music sort of. Some kind of folk music. I have no idea. Some kind of folk music that had been composed recently.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, that's what the music sounded like, the melody.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the -- what about the words? Why do you say it was recently composed folk music?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think it was recently composed folk music. I hadn't heard it before, and there were loudspeakers.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember what they were singing about, what the subject of the songs was?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: No. No, I didn't hear the words, no. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Can the witness please be shown Exhibit 90. That's the excerpt from the institute report.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just -- just take a look at this exhibit. Mr. Petrovic, I think, asked you some questions about the photographs in this report and asked you about the conference you'd had with me just last week and these photographs. Did I -- in this conference, did I give you these photographs and a copy of the report?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did I give you some documents to take away from the conference to look at before you came to court?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes, the statement. The statement, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. I gave you the statement to take away, your statement in Croatian?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you read it after I had given it to you to take away? I think it was last Wednesday.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, fleetingly only.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you still have it?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I think it's in my room.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about these photographs which are in your hand, the report?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: I really don't know. Maybe you did give it to me. I didn't look at it afterwards, not at all really.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just go to the front page, please.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic cross-examined you about your use of the word "guided missile." Please have a look at the front page that says "Type of projectile." The front page of the report, please.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Uh-huh, uh-huh. Yes, yes. I've seen it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic asked you about your use of the words "guided missile." What I wanted to ask you is this: Is this where you have got the words "guided missile" from?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Maybe that reminded me. Perhaps that's how I remembered.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: When you answered Mr. Petrovic and he asked you had you seen the photographs before and you said no, what did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I saw the originals, if I can put it that way. I saw it in the way they actually were.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I don't understand. Can you explain -- what I'm trying to get -- stop, stop. Wait. What Mr. Petrovic asked you -- I asked you questions in examination-in-chief about that report, I took you through the photographs. Mr. Petrovic, in cross-examination, asked you whether you had seen them before and you said no. You've just told us that you think I provided them to you. What I want you to explain to the Trial Chamber is why, when he asked you had you seen them before, you said no. Why did you say no? And what did you mean by "No"?

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: Well, I really didn't look at them. I really didn't. I didn't want to look perhaps. Perhaps that was stronger.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Before you leave that exhibit, I just neglected to do it before. I just want you to sign your name on the bottom of the front and put a date on it, please.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's the 3rd of March.

utterances.speaker: ZINETA OGRESTA
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And have we finished with P89, which is the map, putting the legend on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want to see the legend. Mr. Usher, could you possibly move it to show the Court the legend. It clearly says X - witness's house, A - Mr. Vladimir Srhoj's house, marked on the bottom right-hand corner. Thank you. That concludes my re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mrs. Ogresta, I'm pleased to be able to tell you that that concludes your evidence. You're now free to return to your home. May we thank you for coming and for the assistance that you have given to us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You may now go with the officer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The question arises, Mr. Re, what we do with the remaining few minutes. It would not be practical to start another witness I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: No, Mr. Davies will be the witness in the morning, first thing. Could Your Honours -- could I place on the record that I informed and raised with my learned colleague, Mr. Petrovic, during the break the matter I've just re-examined the witness on in relation to the provision to her of the photographs during the proofing or conferring and the statement, and he was aware of it for the balance of his cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will then adjourn for the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
